LESSON: WRITING 3.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING – POETRY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Writing 3.3.1 Creative Writing – Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.3.1 Creative Writing – Poetry, part of Strand 3 in Grade 9 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: What makes a poem different from a story or a passage?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

4. identify the features (e.g. poet, persona, stanzas and lines) in the poems,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to collect varied poems from the community,
2. organise the poems collected in the class portfolio,
3. conduct a reader’s theatre to read poems on the theme,
4. identify the features (e.g. poet, persona, stanzas and lines) in the poems,
5. work jointly with peers to brainstorm ideas to consider

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.3.1 Creative Writing – Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: The learner exchanges new ideas that inspire creativity when working with peers to compose

and share a short poem on the theme.

• Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner works jointly with peers to brainstorm ideas to consider

when composing a poem on the theme.

Values:
• Unity: It is enhanced as the learner strives to achieve a common goal when working jointly with peers to brainstorm ideas

to consider when composing a poem on the theme – serving the community.

• Peace: It is promoted as the learner displays tolerance when conducting a reader’s theatre to read poems on the theme.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Human rights and Responsibilities: This is enhanced as the learner composes and interacts with poems on serving the

community for societal growth.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of poetry to the composition and performance of poetry in Creative Arts and Sports.
